pin: perl 5.36.3, source archive sha256 f2a1ad88116391a176262dd42dfc52ef22afb40f4c0e9810f15d561e6f1c726a, with this port's seven pointer-layout patches

sysalloc-bounds.what_differs: the first-fit heap as applications get it since PR #170: each allocation bounded, free only marks. THE BASE

sysalloc-sublet.what_differs: the Sublet heap as the SYSTEM allocator: bounded AND every free revokes. Adds temporal safety to the base, at the system allocator only

sublet-svheads.what_differs: CUMULATIVE: the same Sublet system allocator, PLUS the SV head arena through the ports/perl/sv-heads adapter in PERL_SUBLET_MODE=1. PERLD_HEAP=sublet-svheads, which this change added to the port so that one image can carry both -- the analogue of the mruby port's sublet-gc

held_fixed: one source tree, one compiler, one musl, one QEMU, one guest, one staged library; the three images differ only in the heap they link and, for sublet-svheads, the SV head adapter
arm_flag_verified_not_word_split: a flag list passed to cmake as separate words becomes unknown -D cache variables and is silently dropped, which made an mruby control byte-identical to its baseline on 2026-10-05. Checked here three ways: the three image hashes differ, runtime/CMakeCache.txt records CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE='-O1 -DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS=0' as ONE string on the none arm and '-O1' on the baseline, and level0's object file differs between the two
controls: each arm ran two controls before its cases, and the runner EXITS rather than scoring if either fails: the interpreter evaluates 6*7, and the harness loads shim.pl from the staged library. This is not decoration -- the first sublet-svheads attempt scored 11 silences with both controls failing, because the adapter refuses to start without PERL_SUBLET_MODE (PERL-SVH-FAIL code=821)
staged_library_verified: the library is perl's lib/ minus unicore/, auto/ and *.t (47 MiB -> 19 MiB). The prune is not assumed safe: the full 11-case host run with the complete library and with the pruned one give byte-identical verdict tables. An earlier 8-module prune, derived from an %INC probe, silently broke 254b30e378 -- the probe only sees modules in a run that reaches its END block, and that case crashes first
watchdog: 90 s per case; the guest has no timeout(1), so each case carries its own sleeper
node_pool: CAPSTONE_REV_NODES=16777216 on the sublet arm; this kit's emulator does not recycle revocation nodes
launcher: capstone-exec of 2026-10-01 (/tmp/capstone/threads-merge/guest2); CAPSTONE_EXEC_DIAGNOSTICS=1, without which the launcher prints a fault cause only to a tty and a bounds violation cannot be told from a revocation

result.denominator: 10 of 11: only 9e298ab597 fails to execute its defect anywhere but the host

positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.why: three arms reporting the same 6 is exactly what a non-revoking build would also show, so 'sublet is silent on the system-allocator cases' needed a check that the revocation can fire at all. Two questions the eval/shim controls cannot answer
positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.probe: probe/heapprobe.c, compiled with each arm's OWN SDK and run as a domain: malloc, memset, free, then read at an argv-derived index whose value is printed so the load cannot be folded away
positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.sysalloc-bounds: prints READ-FREED-OK got=Z -- the read of freed memory completes, so level0's free does not revoke (l0_free sets b->free = 1 and coalesces, nothing more)
positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.sysalloc-sublet: prints ABOUT-TO-READ-FREED and the process ends there; the read never completes. Revocation is live, so this arm's silence on the system-allocator cases is a fact about those cases
positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.realloc_relocates: both arms print moved=1 for 26->52 and 1000->4000, so a dangling pointer into a grown buffer IS possible here; 'realloc grew in place' was considered and refuted
positive_control_on_the_arms_themselves.why_sysalloc_sublet_still_adds_nothing: the two system-allocator temporal cases it was built for are the two that do not execute their defect in a domain -- 254b30e378's filehandle discards its writes, 9e298ab597's assertion passes. Not a statement about Sublet

library_staging.what_was_wrong: perl-cross installs almost none of the TARGET library: 636 pure-Perl modules the same release installs natively were absent, XSLoader.pm, DynaLoader.pm and PerlIO/scalar.pm among them. Every extension here is linked statically, but perl still reaches an XS layer through its .pm, so PerlIO_find_layer("scalar") could not require PerlIO::scalar and the open fell back SILENTLY to the generic perlio layer
library_staging.how_it_showed: the domain reported `LAYERS perlio` for open($fh, '>', \$str) where the native reference of the same release reports `LAYERS scalar`; writes returned success and the backing scalar stayed undef. It cost 254b30e378 its verdict and would silently degrade any workload needing a module
library_staging.fix: build-perl-domain.sh stages the library from its own native reference, filling only what the cross tree lacks so the target's Config.pm wins, and refuses to continue if XSLoader.pm, DynaLoader.pm or PerlIO/scalar.pm is still missing
library_staging.two_traps_in_writing_that_step: the arch-dependent .pm stubs live under lib/<ver>/<archname>/, so a walk of the version directory alone copies DynaLoader.pm and PerlIO/scalar.pm somewhere @INC never looks -- the fill reports hundreds of files and still leaves the two that matter missing. And detecting that directory by looking for Config.pm in it also matches Net/, because Net::Config exists, which flattens Net/*.pm into the library root; the archname comes from the native perl instead
library_staging.verified: the step's output has ZERO content differences from the library the four arms were measured with, and the domain's layer stack and write behaviour now match the native reference exactly

result_before_the_fix: sysalloc-sublet read 6 and 254b30e378 was recorded as harness_limit. Both were artefacts of the staging and are superseded

cumulative_arm_mechanics.why_it_needed_a_new_heap_mode: one grant has two consumers here, and regions.c's default wrapper for perl returns 0 for region index 0 -- fine for level0, which keeps a static arena, fatal for a Sublet outer heap that needs a real region. Before this change build.py refused the combination outright (--nested with --heap sublet is a ValueError, 'nested discovery arms use level0 for their separate outer heap'), so no single image could carry both protections
cumulative_arm_mechanics.how: PERLD_HEAP=sublet-svheads grants (2 << HEAP_LOG) + 32 MiB and compiles regions.c with EXP_HEAP_AND_POOL, PORT_HEAP_REGION_BYTES and PORT_INNER_REGION_BYTES, linking it with -Wl,--wrap=__capstone_region. That splits the grant: region 0 to the Sublet heap, region 1 to the adapter. It is exactly what ports/mruby/app/build-mruby-domain.sh does for sublet-gc
cumulative_arm_mechanics.verified: the grant reached cmake as 167772160 = (2<<26) + 32 MiB; the linked regions.o is the splitting branch and not the fallback (it references abort, which only EXP_HEAP_AND_POOL does, and is 2184 bytes against the fallback's 1328); the image hash differs from all the others; and the arm passed both of its controls, which a failed region split would not

also_measured_not_an_arm: an unprotected variant (PERLD_SDK_CFLAGS=-DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS=0) catches 6 as well; it differs from the base only in reporting the spatial case b7b77ffc1e as cause 24 (untagged dereference) rather than cause 5 (bounds). Kept as context because the design asks for four arms
superseded: an earlier five-arm set reported sublet-svheads as 7. That build put the adapter over a level0 outer heap, which is not the cumulative arm; it could not see 254b30e378. Superseded by the mode added here
